metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights near Little America, WY
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Little America on I-80 in Sweetwater County, WY? Get a fair cash offer for your checkerboard-pattern interest.
heroLead: Little America is best known as the truck stop and travel plaza off I-80, but the land around it sits squarely in Sweetwater County's checkerboard mineral pattern.
intro: This stretch of southern Wyoming, along the historic transcontinental railroad and now I-80, is where the 1862 Union Pacific land grant left its clearest mark on the map, alternating sections of private and federal ownership that still shape mineral rights today.

sections.heading: Living in the checkerboard's core
paragraphs: If your family's tract near Little America traces to a Union Pacific railroad patent, an odd-numbered section, you likely own the minerals outright alongside the surface. If it traces to a later federal homestead patent, minerals may have been reserved to the government under the Stock-Raising Homestead Act, meaning the BLM owns what's underneath even though you hold the surface.

sections.heading: What's been drilled nearby
paragraphs: Gas activity tied to the Bridger field and similar Sweetwater County trends has periodically extended into this area. Confirming whether your specific section has ever been leased takes a records check, not a guess based on what you can see from I-80.

sections.heading: Selling checkerboard-pattern minerals
paragraphs: First confirm whether you actually own the minerals, private patent or federal reservation, then gather your legal description and any lease history. Sweetwater County Clerk records in Green River hold both patent and lease history for this stretch of the county.

sections.heading: Why the travel plaza doesn't define the mineral picture
paragraphs: Little America's fame as an I-80 stop has nothing to do with the mineral estate underneath the surrounding sections, which follows the same checkerboard patent history as any other tract in this part of Sweetwater County. Don't let the roadside landmark distract from what actually matters: your legal description and patent type.

faqs.question: Do I own the minerals under my Little America-area land?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether your patent traces to the Union Pacific railroad grant or a federal homestead. Check with the Sweetwater County Clerk or BLM records to confirm.

faqs.question: What is the Bridger field and does it reach my tract?
faqs.answer: It's a Sweetwater County tight-gas trend. Whether it reaches your specific section requires checking current lease and unit filings for your legal description.

faqs.question: Can I sell minerals if the BLM owns them instead of me?
faqs.answer: No, you can only sell what you actually own. If your minerals were federally reserved, you'd have nothing to sell regardless of surface ownership.

faqs.question: Does commercial development near Little America affect nearby mineral value?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Mineral value ties to production status, lease history, and geology, not to surface commercial activity like the travel plaza.
